Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League group stage match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City from Saxony. The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

According to recent reports, city, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

In a recent development, for all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

Recent findings suggest that the Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a upcoming proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m.
  • The commissioner introduced the latest player development rule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's substantial game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

Sources indicate that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also unveiled a few fresh league rules and future match events.

Here are the fresh things coming to NWSL:.

The commissioner introduced the latest player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is right now paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

It has been revealed that "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," said Berman in her opening remarks.

Industry observers note that "That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an notable step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the new player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

Sources indicate that the addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also unveiled the fresh NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

According to recent reports, "Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This upcoming year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she stated.

According to recent reports, the NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

Industry observers note that the tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a upcoming community," she said.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

According to recent reports, fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Currently, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite new audiences," Berman said about heading to Austin.

Commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

"Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she said.

Two incoming clubs set for 2028 and new player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

"The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 24 November 2026.

Wesley Fofana has risked the ire of Chelsea fans with an ill-timed interview in which he laughed off his penalty-shootout miss at Liverpool while claiming he considered quitting football while injured until he was convinced otherwise.

The 25-year-old Frenchman, one half of a defence partnership alongside Levi Colwill that has struggled this season, conducted a two-hour chat with a French YouTube channel. It is understood the interview was not arranged by Chelsea, who have lost three of their last four league fixtures and are in an uncomfortable moment under latest manager, Xabi Alonso.

In the discussion, Fofana was asked about the spot-kick he skied at Liverpool which confirmed Chelsea’s exit from the Carabao Cup last month.

According to recent reports, ‘I took responsibility for the penalty. I missed it. I knew I wasn't a good shot from penalties. I (gave away) the penalty in the game. It's a penalty, it's a hand. I could have avoided it.

It has been revealed that ‘You have to go because I'm one of the oldest. On the pitch, there were a lot of young players. You had to take responsibility. ‘If I miss, I've lived through things. It's not that it doesn't matter. For sure, it sucks. But if they attack me, it doesn't matter. It's not the first time they're going to attack me, I don't care. I know that in three days there's another game, they forget you missed a penalty.

Sources indicate that ‘I went, I took it, I missed. I put a nice shot on it. Did you see my shot? I remember a fan really high up caught the ball but yeah, I missed, now I can laugh about it because football is like this. The next game, we beat Man United and that is it.’.

Wesley Fofana risked winding up Chelsea fans with his interview on French YouTube channel.

Fofana smashed his penalty over the bar against Liverpool in October but saw the funny side.

Previously plagued by injuries, Fofana revealed how he considered retirement until he was seemingly advised to honour his contract with Chelsea by his representative.

After taking the points on his driving licence to 50 in January of this year, his lawyer disclosed his salary in a statement to the court, revealing that his client is paid more than £200,000 per week.

He is contracted to Chelsea until 2029.

‘I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. I thought to myself, “I’m too fragile, I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.”.

‘Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream.

‘I sat down with my agents. “I’m not going to play football anymore.” Then they told me about the contract, et cetera.

‘They told me, “It’s not that simple. There are years on your contract to take, there is money to take. Even if you're going to stop playing football, you're going to smile. Even if you get hurt. But you have a contract. You have to finish it. Even for your future.” But I was like, “I don't want it anymore.” In fact, I was like, “Football makes me more unhappy than happy. Why should I continue?”’.

As well as Fofana, Mykhailo Mudryk also conducted an unsolicited interview last week which neither his parent club, Chelsea, nor his loan club, Tottenham Hotspur, knew was happening.

Chelsea’s next match is away at Nottingham Forest this Friday, when Fofana and Colwill, if selected, will need to try to stop their former team-mate Liam Delap from scoring.

Tech Report: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs).
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).
  • The goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text.
  • Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is notable because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

The goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is notable because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The new negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," noted Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

Recent findings suggest that "For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," said Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she mentioned in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

Sources indicate that "Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," remarked Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," said Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

Sources indicate that at 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

"The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," remarked Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

Industry observers note that "The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have mentioned to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text showed a level of "seriousness" on important problems like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

"The question is whether the level of ambition on those concerns is carried through into the final outcome here," mentioned Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us.
  • It has been revealed that while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied.
  • The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a new MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

It has been revealed that while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

It has been revealed that in Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

The parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an issue in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

In the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the Latest England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

Now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

It has been revealed that okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

Industry observers note that hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

Sources indicate that the Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was revealed back in June.

It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Recent findings suggest that just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the big game:.

Recent findings suggest that date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

The Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals rapidly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and new signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit swiftly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman stated of the relationship with her teammates.

"I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but rapidly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

According to recent reports, "I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper said.

"I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she remarked.

In a recent development, the Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

Controversial refereeing decisions have been a part of football for a long as the game has been around, but one of the most bizarre incidents in recent memory occurred during Arsenal’s infamous 6-0 defeat to Chelsea in March 2014.

After spotting an Arsenal handball on the goal line, referee Andrer Marriner reached for his pocket and flashed a red card to Kieran Gibbs.

However, the issue here was that it was actually Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain who had handled the ball, and in this pre-VAR era, Gibbs was forced into an early bath, despite the protests of players from both sides.

As Gibbs looks back on the incident more than a decade on, he remembers the confusion, the frustration and the surreal nature of the incident which wouldn’t be allowed to happen these days.

In a recent development, “It feels like a blur now, and it did at the time too,” he reflects to FourFourTwo. “It’s heated in the moment and you’re trying to focus on the game.”.

The incident came during a calamitous first half for the Gunners, who found themselves 2-0 down after just seven minutes in what was Arsene Wenger’s 1,000th game in charge of the club.

In a recent development, the handball incident came in the 17th minute, when Oxlade-Chamberlain threw his left hand at an Eden Hazard shot, tipping it around the post. Marriner pointed to the spot and the referee was not for turning, despite widespread protests from both sets of players.

The Belgian would slot home the penalty to effectively end the game as a contest, with Gibbs still finding it remarkable that such an incident would occur, given the technology now used in the game.

“It feels crazy that there was no VAR, because you don’t have those kinds of concerns anymore,” he continues.

“It was a surreal and very frustrating moment that was unique in the Premier League, so it brought a lot of attention.

“Both captains and the referee were telling me I was definitely going off.

“After a few minutes of protesting, I needed to listen to them.

“It was a major error from the referee, who apologised later and the red card was rescinded.”.

Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized proposal is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

"I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she said Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

In a recent development, five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

"I'm so excited," she mentioned. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

According to recent reports, "She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan remarked. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

Industry observers note that "We have these significant red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan noted. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

"I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman noted. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many latest players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

"Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone said. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

According to recent reports, "Obviously, it was incredibly crucial for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

Recent findings suggest that "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Fresh York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

"She's fun, she's engaging," Stone noted. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

Rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

It has been revealed that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany.
  • This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?
  • Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany. For the 2029 federal election, it has set itself an ambitious goal: to see its co-chair Alice Weidel to become Germany's next chancellor.

This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?

Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.

"Viewed as a whole, the AfD is an extreme right-wing party that also displays tendencies associated with a fascist movement," said Fabian Virchow, a researcher on right-wing extremism at Düsseldorf University of Applied Sciences, in an interview with DW.

Sources indicate that virchow identifies different factions and strategic tendencies within the party, some of which are at odds with one another. Party leader Alice Weidel, for example, is generally seen as a proponent of a free-market approach that seeks to keep the state as small as possible. Others, by contrast, favor a strong state shaped by an ethnically homogeneous people, among them Björn Höcke, the influential far-right AfD leader in the state of Thuringia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, virchow sees a "normalization" of right-wing extremist positions within the AfD. In his view, this has made the party more attractive to neo-Nazi circles: "Today, many people see greater room for ethnonationalist and radical right-wing ideas.".

Industry observers note that support for this observation comes from the latest findings of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study, one of the most widely cited long-term studies tracking right-wing extremist attitudes in Germany. The researchers behind the study have identified a rise in right-wing extremist views within German society, including a growing acceptance of ideologies rooted in the tradition of National Socialism.

Particularly striking is the finding that around two-thirds of people with firmly entrenched far-right worldviews would vote for the AfD. According to the study, the AfD has achieved what earlier far-right parties in Germany never managed: "to unite large segments of the electorate with anti-democratic attitudes behind it.".

Sources indicate that the debate has been further fueled by several recent incidents within the party. In 2026 alone, numerous AfD politicians and staff members made headlines over alleged ties to neo-Nazi organizations:.

It has been revealed that in August 2026, police carried out a large-scale raid targeting fifteen people. Authorities suspect them of continuing the activities of the so-called "Artgemeinschaft." Before it was banned in 2023, the group was considered one of Germany's largest and most influential neo-Nazi cadre organizations. Particularly explosive was the fact that two of those targeted in the raid are sitting AfD members of the Saxony-Anhalt state parliament. Their attorneys deny the allegations.

According to recent reports, according to reporting by the German daily, Welt, four staff members of the AfD's parliamentary group in Saxony-Anhalt are former members of the now-banned "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" (HDJ), a neo-Nazi youth organization rooted in National Socialist racial ideology that organized paramilitary camps for young people. Two of the staff members held leadership positions within the HDJ and now work closely with AfD politician Ulrich Siegmund, who is seeking to become the AfD's first state premier in December.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Remarkably, both organizations, the "Artgemeinschaft" and the HDJ, are on the AfD's so-called incompatibility list, which is intended to draw a line between the party and extremist organizations and movements. In principle, anyone with a history of membership in such groups is supposed to be excluded from the party.

It has been revealed that but the list appears to be little more than a dead letter. In 2020, former AfD federal executive board member Andreas Kalbitz was expelled from the party after failing to disclose his membership in the "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" on his application to join. Yet according to the news magazine Spiegel, he is once again working for the AfD, this time as a staffer for Saxony-Anhalt state legislator Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, who has since become deputy speaker of the state parliament.

The question of the AfD's relationship to National Socialism has dogged the party since its founding in 2013. Even in its early years, co-founder and first party leader Bernd Lucke sparked controversy when he described democracy and parliamentary politics in Germany as "degenerate," a term the Nazis used to disparage art and culture that did not conform to their ideological worldview.

In Germany, references to the Nazi dictatorship (1933-1945) under Adolf Hitler remain politically taboo because of the country's responsibility for World War Two and the Holocaust, the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If AfD members or their staff have come under scrutiny because of past involvement in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations, they have generally sought to distance themselves from those backgrounds or from the ideologies associated with them.

Sources indicate that but how credible are these attempts at distancing? Laura Neumann* has worked with many people seeking to leave the far-right scene. She works for "Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts," a network of organizations that supports far-right cadres and activists as they disengage from the movement. "A successful exit is the result of a professionally guided process," she said in an interview with DW.

Neumann describes leaving the far-right scene as a challenging process of self-confrontation. "When it comes to someone leaving the movement, the first question I always ask is: How does that person talk about their past? Have they genuinely come to terms with it?".

Based on the experience of exit counselors, one principle generally holds true: the longer and more deeply a person has been immersed in far-right circles, the more difficult it becomes to distance themselves from those beliefs and affiliations.

Recent findings suggest that DW requested a statement from the AfD's federal executive board regarding its handling of party members who were previously active in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations. Individual lawmakers and parliamentary staff members were also asked to comment. None responded.

The party's and its politicians' silence in the face of such allegations reflects an observation made by political scientist Fabian Virchow: "Within the AfD, there is no longer a perceived need to distance oneself from radical far-right positions. That is part of this process of normalization.".

Virchow states that right-wing extremism appears to have advanced so far into the mainstream of German society that efforts to scandalize it now remain largely ineffective.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel described his relationship with Jude Bellingham as being “in a good place” after admitting it had been “a bit up and down”.

Tuchel has two Bellinghams in his latest England squad after calling up Jude’s brother, Jobe, for the first time for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. If they play together, it will be the first time brothers have represented England in the same team since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago.

This time last year, Tuchel cast doubt over Jude’s place in his team by picking Morgan Rogers over him, having not included the Real Madrid midfielder in an England squad the previous month.

But Jude performed superbly for Tuchel at the World Cup and was England’s best player during the last international camp. Tuchel revealed he has listened to his advice by calling up 21-year-old Jobe.

Asked if his relationship with Jude has developed, Tuchel remarked: “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course, but we are in a good place.

Industry observers note that “I love to be his coach, he’s a top player, a very influential player and it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable, he would not perform at that level.

In a recent development, “At the moment, you see he’s happy to come into camp, he’s happy with the role he has, he’s fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them [Bellingham brothers] is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach.”.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Jude once said that playing with Jobe for England would be “the biggest dream of my life” and that it would mean more to him than any trophies.

Industry observers note that “This is also the signal that if you are good in the Under-21s, this is the next step. If you play good for England in the Under-19s, 20s, 21s, if you play good for England in tournaments then it means something.”.

Sources indicate that good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

According to recent reports, whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant concern of note. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

Let's now take a look at the five teams to watch after the break, starting with the Red Devils.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest change of the break: Manchester United sacked coach and club legend Michael Carrick and replaced him with Pochettino, who makes his Premier League comeback after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. As the English giants are right now sitting 18th in the standings, this is a major task for the now-former USMNT head coach, who will make his return at Anfield against Liverpool in his opening game at United. It's a daunting start in one of the most hostile atmospheres in the country. For Pochettino, the challenge will be to strike the right balance between delivering short-term results and laying the foundations for a newly introduced chapter at the club. His ambition will be to usher in a fresh cycle at an institution that has endured one crisis after another since Sir Alex Ferguson stepped down more than a decade ago.

Sources indicate that speaking of a former Manchester United head coach, Jose Mourinho has had some ups and downs early in his first season back at Real Madrid. After winning an exciting away El Clasico match against Barcelona, Mourinho's team is only three points behind Hansi Flick's side right now and is eyeing the possibility of challenging them for the LaLiga title this season. They certainly have all the ingredients to make it happen, particularly following some remarkable additions to the squad in the summer of 2026. Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are arguably entering their prime and appear ready to take the team to the next level, supported by a number of exciting young prospects who could play a key role in shaping the club's future. Will Mourinho be able to win a trophy in his first season back at the club? That would be a story.

According to recent reports, if there is one team to watch in Serie A, it's Como. The side led by Cesc Fabregas is impressing both domestically and in Europe, as it is right now fourth in the league-phase standings of the UEFA Champions League. Fabregas can count on some of the best players in the league, such as Nico Paz, the Argentine talent who is now also expected to lead the national team after Lionel Messi's retirement. The question is how far Como can go this season, given that playing every three days can be a significant challenge for players who have never experienced it. They may still have to pay the price in the league, but qualifying for at least the playoffs of Europe's elite competition would remain a realistic target and, given the circumstances, a remarkable achievement in itself.

It's always about Manchester City: the Citizens are still waiting to learn what sanctions they will face after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. They are facing a challenging season that might have an impact on the years ahead. It's not clear what the sanctions will be, but we will likely know more before the end of the current season. On the pitch, they are also facing a season of changes as longtime coach Pep Guardiola left the club in the summer and was replaced by Enzo Maresca, who is now overseeing that transition.

Sources indicate that spanish soccer is not just about Real Madrid and Barcelona: Atletico Madrid are once again near the top of the standings, five points behind the Blaugrana. Diego Simeone, who has coached the club since 2011, is an Atletico Madrid legend who has faced so many changes over the years but has always been able to recreate the right atmosphere and environment to succeed. Atletico have changed their tactical approach and playing style many times, but they are still near the top, and that is what makes Simeone special.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In recent years, Louisville City FC have been one of the most successful regular-season teams in United Soccer League history, but it hasn't translated to winning the substantial game. They haven't won the USL Championship since 2018, and while this season has been a trying time dealing with injuries and a newly introduced coach taking over, they're playing their best soccer when it matters to set up a strange clash with Sacramento Republic at noon Eastern on Saturday. What's strange isn't that it's Louisville and Sacramento meeting, but that the match kicks off at 9 a.m. local time, a time Louisville forward Ray Serrano states he hasn't played soccer at since he was 15. While it's a regular training time for Louisville and they'll try to keep things on an East Coast timeline, it's hard not to take the shift into account when planning for a final.

Industry observers note that it's a challenge that comes with the desire to reach as many fans as possible with a final of this magnitude. Leagues have to work with broadcast networks to ensure that the slots work, and for the USL, having the game on CBS is worth the risk of a 9 a.m. local start with a West Coast team hosting. It's nothing Louisville won't be prepared for, as they look to keep their internal clocks on Eastern Standard Time.

Recent findings suggest that "No, we're trying to stay on Eastern Time, so for us, it's training time," defender Kyle Adams said. "Wake up at 8:00 a.m., but really it's 5:00 a.m. Go to sleep a little bit earlier. Try to do everything really just to stay on Eastern Time, eat a little bit earlier on the night before, and just treat it as going into training, and then get after them.".

Other teams have dealt with similar complications, like the Los Angeles Rams when playing an NFL game in Australia, but it's still a struggle to deal with en route to a cup final as Louisville look to reach the pinnacle of the sport for the first time since 2018. Winners of the Prinx Tires USL Cup during the regular season, they do have cup experience that will prove to be fruitful in this competition, which Adams noted has been something that brings the injury-riddled squad together. "We know in the last few years we've struggled in these knockout games, but this year we've turned it on," Serrano mentioned. "It has been really good preparation, just the mentality of going into them, how we deal with the pressure, and we're seeing the fruits of all that now.".

It's cliche to say that because of the adversity that they've dealt with, the club is playing its best soccer when it matters, but between using four goalkeepers during the season and seeing manager Danny Cruz depart to be an assistant manager with Minnesota United, it hasn't been an easy task for interim manager Simon Bird to get this team on the right track at this critical juncture.

It has been revealed that "Going back to the main part is the adversity that we've faced. You mentioned injuries, having to deal with that side of it, some of the various parts of the season, different things we've had to deal with from a tactical or technical standpoint, where we've lost games, and we feel that we shouldn't have lost games," Bird mentioned when reflecting on the team's development under his leadership. "The most impressive thing I said to the guys today, yesterday in training, we worked on our defensive structure, but the whole training session I thought was excellent, not just the defensive side, off the ball but with the ball, and to see it all come together towards the end of the season is really rewarding. Hopefully, we can carry that on and put together a complete performance, and that's what we've had throughout the season-moments where we've let ourselves down in all these different areas, set pieces, maybe transition at other times, in front of goal. So, putting it all together for a complete performance on Saturday is the goal.".

Industry observers note that traveling away to a tough environment in Heart Health Park, Louisville will meet the hottest team in the league in Sacramento Republic. They've ridden a club-record 16-game unbeaten run to the final based on their defense. That has set a strong foundation to build on, and it could make the final one where the first team to score a goal wins the match. Sacramento's squad also has experience in USL Cup finals, which goes a long way when preparing for games of this stature.

"I don't think it can hurt to have that. This would be a step forward for my first final. I think experience is invaluable for players and for staff," Sacramento coach Neil Collins remarked. "But then there's also the recognition that every game is different, every team is different, and every season is different. So it's just trying to get the balance right and enjoy the opportunity. You've got to have the mechanisms to control the things you can control. Obviously, the opposition team is trying to do the same, and we've got to do everything we can to be ready to take the opportunity when it comes. But the experience will definitely help us; there's plenty of that in our dressing room.".

It's a final where the best that the league has to offer will be on display, and it couldn't come at a better time. The summer of soccer, with the United States hosting the World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada, has truly turned into a soccer avalanche, and this final showcases one of the top atmospheres in the league. You can't ask for much better than that, as no matter what, a drought will come to an end. Sacramento Republic haven't won the final since 2014, while Louisville haven't won since 2018, and for these clubs, it will mean a lot to get back to the top.

#106370. Industry News: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

Industry News: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios confirmed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.
  • This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.
  • The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios confirmed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

Industry observers note that based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

The first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

In a recent development, in the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

Shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

It has been revealed that in principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their plans.

Sources indicate that although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

Certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

According to recent reports, whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

Sources indicate that aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

In a recent development, another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

Smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

One can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

His pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

Recent findings suggest that in the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

In a recent development, in the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

If there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

Now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

Pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

This article was translated from German by Sarah Hucal. It was first published in 2025 and updated following news of Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond on November 16, 2026.
